tagline: Beside the byway, a railroad bridge carries a different traffic
intro: Gateway to Amish Country follows US 62 and Route 514 through rural countryside. The Federal Highway Administration describes a 30-mile scenic byway with an hour of driving time, highlighting the countryside and the Mohican Valley Trail between Danville and Brinkhaven. That trail parallels the byway on a former railroad corridor.

By the early 1990s, the Pennsylvania Railroad line across the Mohican River had been abandoned. Local residents and businesses planned a multi-use trail, including a roof for its 370-foot railroad bridge. The Bridge of Dreams was completed in December 1998; the Mohican Valley Trail opened in June 2001.

Drive from the Brinkhaven area toward Danville beside the Mohican Valley Trail. Near Brinkhaven, the Bridge of Dreams spans the Mohican River, carrying pedestrians, bicycles and Amish buggies. In Danville, the trail reaches East Street and connects with the Kokosing Gap Trail.

moments.title: Bridge of Dreams
moments.text: The roof came decades after the bridge. Built in the 1920s for the Pennsylvania Railroad, this crossing of the Mohican River became part of a plan to reuse the abandoned line. Local residents and businesses proposed a multi-use trail and a cover for the 370-foot span. The covered bridge was completed in December 1998 and dedicated the following April. It now carries pedestrians and bicycles, and Amish buggies often use it too. Motorized traffic is prohibited. The Mohican Valley Trail opened in June 2001, connecting this reused railroad crossing with a trail from Danville to the Holmes County line.
moments.notice: The 370-foot covered span crosses the Mohican River.

moments.title: Artanna
moments.text: Artanna’s name combines Art and Anna, the familiar names of Arthur and Anna Wolfe. The couple owned a local gas station and, for a time, cabins for travelers in the community.

moments.title: Martinsburg
moments.text: Martinsburg was formed in 1828 when two neighboring rival towns, Hanover and Williamsburg, merged. The village’s beginning belongs to that union of existing communities.
